deliverables.text: A drawn weighted network graph of the corridor: every stop/station a labelled vertex, every segment an edge, every edge labelled with its running time in whole minutes computed as the elapsed time between the two printed clock times in Appendix B; vertex count and edge count stated.

A cycle-and-cut inventory of that graph: the vertices of one cycle written out in order; every edge lying on no cycle listed with the two pieces the network breaks into if it is removed; and one sentence on why Option A exists for the closed edge and not for at least one other listed edge.

A shortest-path table for the five Appendix C trips: shortest path as a vertex sequence plus total weight in minutes, on today's network, the Option A network and the Option B network, with the comparison work that proves minimality.

A rider-minutes ledger: total added rider-minutes per weekday under each option, waiting and in-vehicle minutes on separate lines, then converted to rider-hours per weekday and rider-hours over the whole closure, with a recommendation and a margin.

appendices.title: The Two Service Plans, And How To Count Rider-Minutes

balance.argument_a: The line stays whole and nobody is asked to stand on a platform in January with a bag of groceries waiting for a second vehicle. The published counts say the number of people who would have to do that is small: Line 20's own average trip is 3.4 miles on a route the same report's figures derive to 26.861 miles, so only 12.658% -- 1206.3 of 9530 weekday boardings -- cross the river at all. Option B charges each of those riders 25.107 minutes. Option A charges them only the 2.5-minute detour, and charges everyone else 2.5 minutes of extra wait, the smallest per-person number anywhere in the case. Total: 26840.7 added rider-minutes per weekday against Option B's 30285.8.
balance.argument_b: 2.5 minutes times EVERYBODY is not a small number, and that is the trick of Option A: it looks cheap per person because it is spread across 9530 riders who mostly never go near the bridge -- 23825.0 of its 26840.7 rider-minutes are pure waiting time charged to people whose trip the closure never touched. Option B charges nothing at all to the seven riders in eight who never cross, both halves keep today's 15-minute headway, and the cost lands on the people the closure actually affects. Option B's entire cost rests on one stated assumption rather than a measurement: shorten MA4's east-half extension from 8 minutes to 4 and Option B wins outright by 5.14%. And Option B is the plan that owns its own river crossing -- when the twist closes the detour's own bridge deck, Option A rises to 31665.7 and Option B, unchanged at 30285.8, wins by 4.36%.
balance.margin_basis: Total added rider-minutes per weekday, Option A vs Option B, computed in cases/reroute-wait/sensitivity_model.py from the published running times, headways and ridership in Appendix B/D and the stated plan parameters in Appendix E/G. Margin = (worse - better) / worse.
balance.instability: NOT a stable margin, and the case discloses that fact -- without stating the resulting margin or winner -- in Appendix G MA4 and in case.md's Balance paragraph; the actual numbers are recorded here, in sensitivity_disclosure[] below, and in FACILITATOR.md. Of the three FLEX dials, MA4 (Option B's east-half extension, 8 min) flips the verdict at -50% (B wins by 5.14%) and pushes Option A past the 20% balance cap at +50% (23.55%). MA2 and MA3 do not flip it. The twist also flips it, by design.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: Option B's east-half bus extension (E Burnside & SE 12th to Rose Quarter TC) does not operate today, so its true running time cannot be directly measured or cited -- it is a good-faith estimate built from the closest public analogue, Line 20's own published pace over the comparable ~1-mile segment from E Burnside & SE 12th to E Burnside & Cesar Chavez (8 minutes, source S2). This is a one-time proprietary/inaccessible exception, not a substitute for real sourcing, and it is the single dial that flips the verdict at -50% and breaches the SPEC section 2 20% cap at +50%.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Part of Option A's definition, not a measurement: detour every bus and hold the fleet fixed. A longer round trip on a fixed fleet buys a wider headway, and 20 is the next standard clock-face step above 15.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: EXCLUDED from the FLEX sweep as a plan parameter, not an uncertain quantity. Handed to the room directly at FACILITATOR.md Anchor 4 instead.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Option A's extra in-vehicle time for a crossing rider
modeling_assumptions.basis: Priced at the closed segment's own published pace [S2] rather than guessed: about six tenths of a mile added to a segment the timetable covers in 6 minutes over about a mile and a half.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Swept +/-50%: A by 16.35% at 1.25 min, A by 6.40% at 3.75 min. Does not flip.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Walking distance, Pioneer Square North to W Burnside & SW 5th
modeling_assumptions.basis: Three downtown Portland blocks. Converted to minutes at the cited pedestrian design speed [S8].
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Swept +/-50%: A by 6.03% at 300 ft, A by 16.15% at 900 ft. Does not flip.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Running time of Option B's east-half extension, E Burnside & SE 12th to Rose Quarter TC
modeling_assumptions.basis: About one mile of inner-eastside city street, priced at Line 20's own published pace [S2] rather than an outside estimate.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: THE DIAL THAT FLIPS THE CASE. Swept +/-50%: at 4 min Option B wins by 5.14%; at 12 min Option A leads by 23.55%, past the SPEC section 2 20% cap. Declared in balance.instability and in FACILITATOR.md.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Case data cutoff, and closure length
modeling_assumptions.value_used: Ridership frozen at Spring 2024 [S1] and Spring 2025 station census [S7]; schedules frozen as retrieved 2026-08-12 [S2,S3,S4]; closure length five years = 1,300 weekdays at 260 weekdays/year
modeling_assumptions.basis: SPEC section 5 'as of' rule. TriMet's schedules and counts keep moving on three different cycles and the county page's printed start year is stale [S6]; every figure is pinned to the vintage named beside it and none is refreshed independently.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Closure length scales both options identically and cannot change the winner; it changes only the size of the number reported.

modeling_assumptions.value_used: share crossing an interior point = average trip length / route one-way length = 3.4 / 26.861 = 12.658%
modeling_assumptions.basis: Standard result for trips scattered uniformly along a line. Consumes only sourced figures.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Stated rather than swept, because every number it consumes is sourced. Known direction of error: the closed edge sits nearer the middle of the route and in its densest stretch, so the true share is probably HIGHER, which pushes against Option A — the plan the arithmetic favours.

sensitivity_note: SPEC section 6: no sensitive-subject flag required. The stake is access -- minutes of a rider's day -- not illness, death, money stress or family hardship. Guide note: keep the discussion on what is owed to the riders who cross, rather than treating 1206.3 people as an abstract quantity to minimise.

cohort_bands.note: Socratic plan and anchor timings run as written in FACILITATOR.md (0:00-45:00). Anchor 1 vote is a real show-of-hands split; all three deep-conflict threads run; the graph is drawn on a shared board so the room argues over one drawing.

Anchors 2 and 3 combine into one pass ('who actually pays, and in what units'). Run only one deep-conflict thread (flat cost vs targeted cost) at 20:00-30:00. Twist still drops at 15:00. Total runtime ~30 min. Draw the graph together rather than comparing separately-drawn graphs.

No vote to take at Anchor 1 - the learner states an initial position instead. The guide argues the other side directly rather than cold-calling. Skip the deep-conflict threads; go straight from twist-recommit to Close. Have the learner re-derive the crossing share aloud, since there is no room to catch an error in it.
